en: The *Kulika-rāja-nāga-vidhi* was composed by the Tripiṭaka Master Vajrabodhi for those of the most superior faculties to manifest in this very life; alternatively, it may be used for binding [the deity] and for the practice of recitation.
This must necessarily manifest in form;
it is merely the manifestation of the three poisons and afflictions during the causal stage of the Tathāgata Mahāvairocana.
At that time, the Tathāgata Mahāvairocana, the Vajra-Wrathful Warriors, the various devas, and others—
For those who practice for my sake, I manifest in the form of the Wrathful Dragon King;
through fear of his three poisons and afflictions,
they shall forever leave behind the suffering karma of the three realms of cyclic existence.
For this reason, one may speak my secret mantra.
The mantra is: Oṃ āḥ hūṃ.
Next is the manifestation-body mudrā and mantra of the Nāga King Kulika.
With both hands forming the wrathful gesture, raise both shoulders.
The mantra is: Oṃ Vajra-hūṃ.
Next is the mantra and mudrā of Acala Vidyārāja and the Nāga King Kujaku.
Form the two hands into the vajra-clasp (*vajra-añjali*).
Open and spread the two index fingers and the two middle fingers.
Insert the two little fingers into the palms.
Mantra: [OṂ] HŪṂ SVĀHĀ.
The Heart-to-Heart Mudrā: Form the inner fist by joining the two water fingers and the two fire fingers, then open and spread them apart.
The Heart-to-Heart Mantra is as follows:
􄚳􄩟􄭑􈁟􄙢􆿅􈁝􄕞􈁅􇖴. This is the Fundamental Manifestation Mantra of Acala Tathāgata, Mahāvairocana Tathāgata, and the Dragon King. 􈁴􄩟􄙖􄙊􄗯􄚦􆿆􇖴. Recite this mantra.
One will certainly manifest one’s rebirth in the pure lands of the ten directions.
If one pays homage to this sacred image,
until reaching Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi, one shall never fall into the three evil realms.
This is the supernatural power of the Dragon King’s Samādhi of Fiery Radiance (*jvālana-samādhi*).
As for the Fire Deity (*Agnideva*), he is so called because he is spoken of by means of the four wisdoms (*catur-jñāna*).
The venerable Fire Deity’s magnificent radiance within the Samādhi of Fiery Radiance is entirely the body of this Fire Deity.
One should be able to contemplate this inconceivable supernatural power of the Dragon King.

There is only this method: by contemplating the *dharmatā* of the original birth, one transforms the Great Sun (*Vairocana*) into Acala, transforms Acala into the supreme mark of the sword—the letter *Aṃ*, which in turn becomes the Dragon King.
The left and right ring fingers and little fingers are interlaced within the palms;
the two middle fingers stand upright and touch one another;
and the two index fingers rest upon the third phalanges of the backs of the middle fingers.
With the two thumbs slightly bent, each supports the inner middle joints of the two index fingers, moving them back and forth.
*Namo samantabuddhānāṃ kuli-kāya-karāja-miṅga-śanaye svāhā*. Next is the secret mantra-seal for the Naga King Kulika.
Bind the two middle fingers inward;
spread the two thumbs apart—this is the secret mudrā.
Next is the *Kulika-rūpavikāra-mudrā-mantra* of Mahāvairocana Tathāgata: 􄖩􄗰􄙺􄗥􆩖􆿁􈁅􇖴.
Join the two hands in *añjali*.
The two *vāyu* (wind) fingers and the two *ākāśa* (space) fingers should touch their tips;
the two *ap* (water) fingers stand apart.
The mantra is: Oṃ vajra-maye vajra [svāhā]. Next is the mantra and mudrā of the Vajra-body.
Oṃ haṃ hūṃ vajra-maye vajra [svāhā]. Next is the ocean-samādhi mudrā and mantra.
Oṃ vajrasakha. Next, the mantra for the mudrā of the Constantly Abiding Fire-Light Samādhi is:
Oṃ vajrasakha haṃ. If a practitioner constantly maintains mindfulness of this Kuliśa Nāgarāja, [he shall attain success].
The *homa* fire-light samādhi is spontaneously accomplished.
All the four-armed Vidyārājas constantly spread the power of this nāga king over the body of the practitioner; within it is the letter A (𑀅), which universally contains the five syllables. 𑀅.
One’s entire body becomes the vajra-body of Acala.
Having visualized thus, one recites the single-syllable mantra:
*Namaḥ samantavajrāya haṃ*. Next is the mantra for the *kaniṣṭhā-mudrā*, which is *śakara*. This is it.
Form the Vajra-joined palms with both hands;
inserting the two middle fingers and the two thumbs into the palms constitutes the mantra.
Oṃ kankāla-vajra. Next is the *śitaka* seal and mantra.
With the two hands bound within, the two earth and two wind fingers are opened and slightly curved to form the seal.
Oṃ vajra śe hūṃ khid-ta-ka-ya svāhā. This is the mantra of the Lotus Śrī Seal; Avalokiteśvara is the Lord of this Family.
Join the two palms together.
Interlace the two water and two wind fingers within.
*Namo samanta-vajrāya hūṃ hūṃ haṃ ye dhāraya svāhā*. These four messengers, when joined with Acala, become the five messengers.
This is the formation of the body of Mahāvairocana through the five wisdoms. The *Kulakalpa-vidhi*.
